title: Notre environnement naturel
oneGoal: Students will identify different natural environments around them and recognize that they are part of these environments
decisionPoints: What natural environments are familiar to students in their local area?
Should we start with outdoor exploration or indoor observation of nature pictures?
Are students ready to understand that they are part of the environment?
progression: Foundation lesson - introduces the concept of environment and establishes students as active participants
realWorldConnection: Recognizing the parks, forests, beaches, or gardens in their neighborhood as natural environments

title: Les animaux dans leur maison naturelle
oneGoal: Students will observe and identify where different animals live in natural environments
decisionPoints: Which local animals and their homes are most visible to students?
Should we focus on one habitat type or compare different animal homes?
Are students ready for simple habitat matching activities?
progression: Builds on Lesson 1 by exploring how animals are connected to specific natural environments
realWorldConnection: Understanding where birds build nests, where squirrels live, and where fish swim

title: Les plantes ont leur place aussi
oneGoal: Students will identify where different plants grow naturally and why location matters for plants
decisionPoints: Which plant examples show clear location preferences (water plants, shade plants)?
Should we use classroom plants or outdoor examples for observation?
Are students ready to connect plant location to plant needs?
progression: Builds on Lesson 2 by expanding habitat understanding to include plants and their environmental needs
realWorldConnection: Noticing why certain plants grow in gardens, forests, or near water

title: Tout est connecté dans la nature
oneGoal: Students will discover simple connections between animals, plants, and their environment
decisionPoints: Which nature connections are most concrete for Grade 1 understanding?
Should we focus on food connections or shelter connections first?
Are students ready for simple cause-and-effect thinking about nature?
progression: Builds on Lesson 3 by introducing the concept that living things depend on each other and their environment
realWorldConnection: Understanding how birds need trees for nests and trees need birds to spread seeds

title: L'eau: source de vie partout
oneGoal: Students will recognize that all living things need clean water and identify water sources in nature
decisionPoints: Which water sources are accessible for student observation?
Should we discuss clean vs dirty water or focus only on natural water sources?
Are students ready to understand water as a shared resource?
progression: Builds on Lesson 4 by focusing on water as a critical connection point for all living things
realWorldConnection: Recognizing rivers, lakes, rain, and drinking water as essential for all life

title: L'air pur pour tous les vivants
oneGoal: Students will understand that all living things need clean air and identify what helps keep air clean
decisionPoints: How can we make air quality visible and understandable for young students?
Should we focus on trees helping air or on avoiding air pollution?
Are students ready for simple discussions about air quality?
progression: Builds on Lesson 5 by exploring air as another shared environmental resource needed by all
realWorldConnection: Understanding why trees are important and why we avoid polluting the air

title: Prendre soin de notre environnement
oneGoal: Students will identify simple ways they can help take care of their natural environment
decisionPoints: Which environmental care actions are age-appropriate and actionable for students?
Should we focus on individual actions or group environmental projects?
Are students ready for responsibility discussions about environmental care?
progression: Builds on Lesson 6 by empowering students to become active environmental caretakers
realWorldConnection: Learning how picking up litter, not disturbing animals, and caring for plants helps everyone

title: Réduire nos déchets
oneGoal: Students will understand that making less waste helps protect the environment and identify ways to reduce waste
decisionPoints: Which waste reduction concepts are most concrete for Grade 1 students?
Should we focus on household waste or classroom waste examples?
Are students ready for before-and-after comparisons of waste reduction?
progression: Builds on Lesson 7 by introducing waste reduction as a key environmental care strategy
realWorldConnection: Understanding how using both sides of paper and bringing reusable water bottles helps nature

title: Réutiliser les objets créativement
oneGoal: Students will discover how to give objects new purposes instead of throwing them away
decisionPoints: Which reuse projects are safe and achievable for Grade 1 students?
Should we focus on art projects or functional reuse examples?
Are students ready for creative problem-solving with waste materials?
progression: Builds on Lesson 8 by providing practical alternatives to throwing things away
realWorldConnection: Learning how empty containers can become plant pots and old clothes can become cleaning rags

title: Le recyclage: donner une nouvelle vie
oneGoal: Students will understand how recycling transforms old materials into new products
decisionPoints: Which recycling examples are most visible and understandable to students?
Should we focus on paper recycling or multiple material types?
Are students ready for simple sorting activities with recyclable materials?
progression: Builds on Lesson 9 by introducing recycling as a transformation process that helps the environment
realWorldConnection: Understanding how paper becomes new paper and bottles become new products

title: Trier pour mieux recycler
oneGoal: Students will learn to sort different materials for recycling and understand why sorting helps
decisionPoints: Which materials are safest for student sorting activities?
Should we use real recyclables or picture sorting for this lesson?
Are students ready for multi-category sorting tasks?
progression: Builds on Lesson 10 by developing practical recycling skills through sorting and categorizing
realWorldConnection: Learning why families have different bins for paper, plastic, and other recyclables

title: Les 3 R: Réduire, Réutiliser, Recycler
oneGoal: Students will understand and apply the 3 Rs as a strategy for helping the environment
decisionPoints: How can we make the 3 Rs sequence memorable and actionable for students?
Should we focus on one R at a time or present them as an integrated approach?
Are students ready for priority thinking (reduce first, then reuse, then recycle)?
progression: Builds on Lesson 11 by consolidating waste reduction concepts into a memorable framework
realWorldConnection: Having a simple strategy to follow when deciding what to do with items at home and school

title: Notre projet de compostage
oneGoal: Students will create a simple compost system and understand how food scraps become soil
decisionPoints: What type of composting system is appropriate for classroom use?
Should we focus on the decomposition process or the end result of rich soil?
Are students ready for long-term observation of decomposition changes?
progression: Builds on Lesson 12 by introducing composting as another way to handle organic waste naturally
realWorldConnection: Understanding how kitchen scraps can help garden plants grow better

title: Économiser l'énergie ensemble
oneGoal: Students will identify simple ways to save energy at home and school to help the environment
decisionPoints: Which energy conservation actions are within student control and understanding?
Should we focus on electricity, heat, or transportation energy?
Are students ready to understand the connection between energy use and environment?
progression: Builds on Lesson 13 by expanding environmental care to include energy conservation
realWorldConnection: Learning why turning off lights and using less hot water helps protect nature

title: Créer un jardin pour les pollinisateurs
oneGoal: Students will plant flowers to help bees and butterflies and understand how this helps the ecosystem
decisionPoints: Which flowers are most likely to attract pollinators in our local area?
Should we focus on container gardening or ground planting?
Are students ready to understand the pollinator-plant relationship?
progression: Builds on Lesson 14 by creating positive environmental action through habitat creation
realWorldConnection: Understanding how helping bees and butterflies helps flowers and food grow

title: Les transports respectueux de l'environnement
oneGoal: Students will identify transportation choices that help keep air and environment clean
decisionPoints: Which transportation examples are most relevant to student experiences?
Should we focus on walking/biking benefits or reducing car use?
Are students ready for simple cause-and-effect discussions about transportation and air quality?
progression: Builds on Lesson 15 by exploring how daily choices about transportation affect the shared environment
realWorldConnection: Understanding why walking to school or taking the bus can help keep air clean

title: Protéger les animaux sauvages
oneGoal: Students will learn respectful ways to observe and protect wild animals in their natural habitats
decisionPoints: Which wildlife protection concepts are appropriate for Grade 1 safety and understanding?
Should we focus on observing from distance or protecting animal homes?
Are students ready for discussions about human impact on wildlife?
progression: Builds on Lesson 16 by developing respectful relationships with wildlife as part of environmental stewardship
realWorldConnection: Learning how to watch birds and animals safely without disturbing their homes

title: Partager notre planète équitablement
oneGoal: Students will understand that all living things need space and resources and practice sharing environmental spaces
decisionPoints: How can we make environmental sharing concepts concrete for Grade 1 students?
Should we focus on playground sharing or broader environmental sharing?
Are students ready for fairness discussions related to environmental resources?
progression: Builds on Lesson 17 by developing understanding of environmental justice and fair sharing of natural resources
realWorldConnection: Understanding why everyone needs access to clean parks, water, and natural spaces

title: Devenir des ambassadeurs de l'environnement
oneGoal: Students will teach others about caring for the environment and share their environmental knowledge
decisionPoints: What teaching format works best for Grade 1 students to share environmental knowledge?
Should students focus on one environmental topic or share multiple learning points?
Are students ready for peer and family teaching responsibilities?
progression: Builds on Lesson 18 by empowering students to become environmental leaders and educators
realWorldConnection: Building confidence to teach family members about environmental care actions

title: Célébration de notre environnement partagé
oneGoal: Students will celebrate their environmental learning by showcasing actions they've taken and commitments for the future
decisionPoints: How can the celebration highlight each student's environmental contributions?
Should we include environmental displays, action demonstrations, or both?
What activities best show student growth in environmental awareness to families?
progression: Culmination of all previous lessons - celebrates environmental stewardship learning while building ongoing commitment to environmental care
realWorldConnection: Sharing our environmental care actions with families and community to inspire continued environmental protection
